how: Matsuriza Taiko, a metro Atlanta Japanese drum troupe, performs at JapanFest and community events, but no regular open beginner classes were confirmed.
The Chado Urasenke Tankoukai Atlanta Association meets at Nakato Restaurant and tea ceremony workshops appear at the annual JapanFest.
Chastain Arts Center's pottery studio runs eight-to-nine-week wheel-throwing courses for beginners and intermediate students on weekday and weekend slots.
INDIEHOUSE runs guided custom-perfume workshops using professional perfumer's oils, with each guest taking home a 30 ml bottle.
Atlanta Irish Dance by Burke Connolly teaches Irish dance to all ages and abilities at its Faulkner Road studio and branches in Marietta, Decatur and Sandy Springs.
1 Dot Mah Jongg, Two Sparrows and Atlanta Mahjong Studio run lessons, guided play and leagues, and a Decatur social club hosts supervised beginner games.
Boat Rock, a granite bouldering area southwest of the city, offers hundreds of boulder problems in the Greater Atlanta area, with classics such as Yellow Wall Arete.
Stone Mountain Park hosts long-running caches including the multi-cache tour of Stone Mountain, and Atlanta has thousands of caches in city parks.
Stone Mountain Park offers a campground plus yurt rental sites inside the park.
Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area offers ranger-led hikes, and Chattahoochee Nature Center runs trail and education programs.
The Georgia Orienteering Club holds regular park events with a beginner guide, though many courses are in state parks beyond the metro radius.
Chattahoochee Nature Center in Roswell has licensed wildlife staff rehabilitating birds of prey with resident raptors on display, plus riverside trails for wild hawks.
No beach exists in the metro area, but Chattahoochee Riverkeeper's annual Sweep the Hooch river cleanup has dozens of sites in Metro Atlanta counties and the national recreation area.
The National Archives at Atlanta in Morrow holds federal records for eight southeastern states, with a research room open by appointment.
Meetup lists large Atlanta groups for hiking, board games, mahjong, crafts and journaling, with weekly events.
Opo Coffee Training Lab in Decatur runs small beginner latte-art classes led by an SCA-authorized trainer.
The APEX Museum on Sweet Auburn Avenue preserves and presents Black history with exhibits on the Sweet Auburn district.
The Atlanta Writers Club holds monthly meetings and periodic workshops, with critique groups across the metro and a free first visit.
Cozymeal and Classbento list chef-led Chinese and dumpling-making classes in Atlanta covering folding techniques and dim sum menus.
Atlanta Botanical Garden runs Sourdough 101 classes where each student takes home a starter, and The Cook's Warehouse in Midtown offers hands-on sourdough classes.
XOCOLATL Small Batch Chocolate at Krog Street Market offers micro-factory tours and bean-to-bar tastings, though hands-on making classes were not confirmed as ongoing.
Cultured South, a kombucha taproom on the BeltLine Westside Trail, hosts occasional fermentation classes and Atlanta Utility Works runs hands-on fermentation events.
Local teachers run beginner to advanced Argentine tango classes through Meetup and a weekly class at Daza Dance on Peachtree Road.
Georgia Tech's RotorJackets host MultiGP regional qualifier races at Couch Park Field, and the DRC Atlanta chapter races FPV drones.
Atlanta SUP Yoga holds seasonal sessions, including night classes, on Lake Lanier and earlier reports mention classes at Morgan Falls on the Chattahoochee.
Atlanta GAA (Clan na nGael), founded in 1996, fields men's and women's Gaelic football, hurling and camogie teams and runs a coed league.
Atlanta has hundreds of community gardens with rentable plots, including Blue Heron Community Garden's 30-plus organic plots and city park plots reserved through Atlanta Recreation.
The Urban Food Forest at Browns Mill, Atlanta's first food forest, allows visitor foraging including mushrooms, though no organised mushroom forays were confirmed.
venue: Urban Food Forest at Browns Mill

how: Language Exchange Atlanta meets every other Sunday on Buford Highway in Doraville, splitting members into practice groups by language.
A Philosophy Cafe discussion group meets monthly at Moe's in Buckhead, listed on Philosophy Now's events page.
Buckhead, Peachtree and iNCRedible Toastmasters clubs meet weekly in Atlanta, and guests can usually visit free.
Library and cultural-centre workshops such as a Fulton County Library calligraphy session at Buckhead Library offer one-off Chinese calligraphy, with no regular class confirmed.
TuTu Tufting on Peachtree Road runs rug-tufting and other fluid-art activities.
Atlanta History Center hosted the Their Finest Hour WWII exhibit (closed March 2026) and traveling WWII exhibits, and holds the Veterans History Project oral histories.
Lion and dragon dances are performed at metro Atlanta Chinese New Year events, though no regular lion-dance class was confirmed.
venue: Metro Atlanta Chinese New Year events

how: No drop zone operates inside the metro area because of airspace and safety constraints; the nearest tandem operator, Skydive Monroe at Monroe-Walton County Airport, is about an hour east of Atlanta.
Cherrylion Studios in Atlanta teaches classical and contemporary sculpting in clay, plaster and other media to adults and teens, from basic forms to finished works.
Epicurean Atlanta hosted a two-hour Coffee Connoisseur class with a master roaster and live roasting demonstration, though the latest listing found was from 2023.
Vino Venue has listed a WSET introductory sake course and Savi Provisions in Inman Park has hosted sake festivals with over 30 sakes to taste.
The Meadow at Piedmont Park hosts the annual Atlanta World Kite Festival and Expo, and the open park is used for casual kite flying year-round.
BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Lilburn, among the largest Hindu temples in the US, is open free to visitors daily with a daily Arti ritual.
The flat Piedmont terrain around Atlanta has no soaring sites; the nearest flight park is Lookout Mountain Flight Park at Rising Fawn, Georgia, roughly two hours' drive northwest.
No luge track exists in the Southeast; the nearest permanent tracks are in Lake Placid, New York and Park City, Utah, and Atlanta's climate rules out natural-track sliding.
Buzkashi is a Central Asian horseback game played mainly in Afghanistan and neighbouring countries, with no organised play in Georgia.
No bathing hot springs exist in the metro area; the nearest natural warm springs are at Warm Springs, Georgia, about 90 minutes south, and the region's geology offers none closer.
